summary.title: On Software Architecture, Programming Languages, Engineering Management, and Systems Thinking
summary.one_liner: A blog index by Lutz Huehnken covering event-driven architecture, reactive systems, and JVM languages like Scala, Java, Kotlin and Flix.
takeaways: Events can be emitted by one service and consumed by many, or the reverse (many-to-one), and each direction has different design implications.
Event-driven architecture is not all-or-nothing; an event-driven core can sit behind a request-response shell such as REST.
Different asynchronous communication styles have different characteristics and impact system structure.
Project Loom adds lightweight virtual threads to the JDK; Flix and Scala features are covered for Java developers.
Avoid blocking on asynchronous I/O in Scala with Await.result.
summary.summary: This is the index page of Lutz Huehnken's personal blog, listing short posts on event-driven architecture, reactive systems, and software engineering. Several posts focus on event design, such as the dual nature of events, common misconceptions, and distinguishing event collaboration from event sourcing. Other posts compare JVM languages (Java, Scala, Kotlin, Flix) and cover Project Loom and reactive-systems pitfalls for Java developers. The page itself contains only post titles and one-line teasers, so the details live in the linked articles.
